notes: No external resistor: pin 2 uses the internal pull-up (INPUT_PULLUP). Pin 13 drives the onboard LED only, so no external LED or wire is added.
Breadboard bank naming follows the catalogue: 't' is rows a-e and 'b' is rows f-j. In the image the button straddles the centre gap, with its legs in columns 10 and 12 (rows f and e).
The pushbutton's 1.l/1.r are the column-10 legs (joined inside). 2.l/2.r are the column-12 legs. Which leg is called l or r is arbitrary.

The teal wire goes from pin 2 to column 10 (row c). The black wire goes from column 12 (row c) to a GND pin on the power header. I chose GND.2 because the image shows the lower of the two GND pins on that header.
The breadboard power rails are not used.
The circuit image is the authority; the schematic shows pin 2 but the text and breadboard image use pin 4, so pin 4 is used.

The breadboard image is drawn with rows f-j in the upper half and a-e in the lower half. The catalogue puts rows a-e in bank 't'. The lower half of the image is therefore mapped to bank 't' and the upper half to bank 'b'.
The pushbutton straddles the centre gap. Side 1 is column 6 (1.l at 6b.f, 1.r at 6t.e) and side 2 is column 8 (2.l at 8b.f, 2.r at 8t.e).
The pin 4 wire and the resistor's top leg are both in column 6. The short red wire is in column 8 and runs to the lower + rail.

The lower rails are mapped as bottom-row negative = 'bn' and + = 'bp'. The exact rail hole numbers (bp.2, bp.6, bn.1, bn.5) are estimated from the picture. Any hole on the same rail is electrically equivalent.
The resistor is 10 kΩ, set as value=10000. It acts as a pull-down from pin 4 to GND.
The USB cable to the computer is not drawn in the circuit image, so it is not included.
Wiring follows the circuit image and schematic: 5V->VCC, A0->VERT, A1->HORZ, pin 6->SEL, GND->GND.

In the image the five joystick pins sit in one breadboard column, which would short them. I put each pin in its own column (8t to 12t, row e), with one jumper wire per pin in row a of the same column.
Breadboard hole names follow the catalogue (top half = rows a-e), not the j-f labels printed in the image.

The optional status LED on pin 5 is included: pin 5 -> 220 ohm resistor -> LED anode, LED cathode -> GND. Its GND return goes to Leonardo GND.2, which is my assumption. The manual gives no layout for it.
The optional second pushbutton (left click on D3, 10k pulldown) is not built. The manual only points to the button circuit page for it.
The joystick's built-in pushbutton is the SEL pin, so no pulldown resistor is used on pin 6.
The USB cable to the computer is not modelled.
Matrix pins are mapped to the catalogue's R1-R8 / C1-C8 ports using the manual's pin table (row/column numbers), not the physical pin numbers.
Wire colours follow the circuit image: green wires go straight from the Uno to the matrix, yellow wires pass through 1k resistors.
The 8 resistor chains are modelled as Arduino pin -> wire -> resistor -> wire -> matrix pin, since the image shows resistors inline in the yellow wires.

Breadboard hole names and rail hole numbers are approximate readings of the image. The top-half rails (tp/tn) stand in for the right-hand power rails. The two pots sit across the centre gap, with the wiper on the left (bank t) and the outer legs on the right (bank b). Short jumpers carry the outer legs to the + and - rails.
Pot1 (upper) wiper goes to A1 and pot2 (lower) wiper goes to A0, as in the image. The manual says only that pots are on A0 and A1.
The 5V and GND wires from the Uno feed the breadboard rails, which supply the pots. The matrix is driven from Arduino pins only.
Resistor value 1k is entered as value=1000 (ohms) to match the catalogue's resistor value convention.
